purpose: The v2 scenarios (same machines, true causes, alternatives and discriminators as scenarios.json) with an added `intake` block per scenario: the fields an operator would realistically have already typed on the intake form before the interview starts — recent service/fluid changes, a fuel-source change, jobsite/duty-cycle context, serial/PIN — written short and plain, in the operator's own voice. Used ONLY for the UXT-11 arm (evals/prompt-variants/uxt-11.mjs), which tests whether the interview stops re-asking what intake already collected. Every fact moved into `intake` was deleted from that scenario's `hiddenFacts` so it can never be 'revealed' twice by the operator simulator; every alternative's discriminator, and the true-root-cause tell itself, stayed in `hiddenFacts` and remains reachable only by asking. Deliberately NOT comparable to the frozen `scenarios.json` baseline — the simulated operator here starts by handing over evidence the baseline runs never had. DECONTAMINATED 2026-08-15: an intake string may set up a specific follow-up but must never contain the operative clause of trueRootCause or of any alternative discriminator. Cases 05 and 10 violated that and were rewritten; their tells moved back into hiddenFacts. Runs before this change are NOT comparable to runs after it.

scenarios.surfaceProblem: Hard to start in the morning — cranks a long time with a bunch of white smoke before it catches. Once it's running it's fine all day, and warm restarts are instant.
scenarios.trueRootCause: Failed glow plugs (two of four dead) — long cranks with white smoke when cold, instant starts warm.

alternatives.discriminator: Cranking speed is strong and normal; lights stay bright while cranking.
Happens even on mild 50°F mornings, fuel from the same co-op source for years, no filter issues.
Instant warm starts, full power once running, no blow-by or oil use — a compression problem doesn't vanish when warm.

hiddenFacts: Cranks fast and strong — battery and starter sound healthy, lights stay bright.
Lots of white smoke while cranking cold; smoke clears once it finally catches.
Happens even on mild mornings around 50°F, worse when colder.
Warm restarts are instant all day. Full power, no oil consumption, no blow-by.
Fuel from the same farm co-op for years; filter changed at last service 150 hours ago.
The glow plug indicator light on the dash goes out after a few seconds like always.
No fault codes.

intake.operatingConditions: Working a grain elevator site — real dusty this time of year.
intake.recentWork: Coolant and belts are original. We keep up with the regular service on it, nothing skipped.

scenarios.surfaceProblem: Engine temp climbs into the red after 30-45 minutes of hard pushing. If I back off and idle a few minutes it comes right back down. Getting worse the last few weeks.
scenarios.trueRootCause: Radiator and hydraulic cooler fins packed with dust and chaff — heat rejection fine at low load, overwhelmed under sustained load.

alternatives.discriminator: A stuck thermostat overheats quickly regardless of load, even idling — this machine idles cool all day and only climbs under sustained hard work, then recovers at idle.
Coolant level never drops, no leaks, no coolant smell — and idle temperature is normal.
No coolant loss, no white exhaust, no bubbles in the reservoir, oil clean.

hiddenFacts: Only overheats under sustained heavy pushing; idles and light work stay at normal temp; recovers within minutes at idle.
Coolant level has not dropped all month; reservoir at the same mark every morning.
The radiator screen and fins are visibly caked with dust — never blown out.
Oil is clean, no white smoke, no sweet smell, no bubbles in the reservoir.
No fault codes read.

intake.operatingConditions: Sits locked up in the yard overnight.

scenarios.surfaceProblem: Battery's stone dead every morning. Jump it and it runs perfect all day, charges up, starts fine at lunch. Park it overnight and it's dead again.
scenarios.trueRootCause: Parasitic draw — an aftermarket LED beacon/work-light kit wired unswitched (always hot) about two months ago drains the battery overnight.

alternatives.discriminator: Voltmeter shows ~14V running and the battery recovers enough during the day for a warm restart — charging is happening.
Battery is 6 months old and load-tested good at the parts store last week.
Key comes out every night, panel dark when parked — but the beacon kit added two months ago is wired straight to the battery.

hiddenFacts: Dash voltmeter reads about 14V while running; battery recharges during the day and restarts fine at lunch.
Battery is 6 months old, load-tested good at the parts store last week.
Key removed every night; panel and lights off when parked.
An LED beacon and extra work-light kit was installed by a helper about two months ago, wired straight to the battery — the drain started around then.
No other electrical work ever done. No blown fuses.

intake.operatingConditions: Loads out of a dusty limestone pit all day. Same fuel supplier for years, no issues there.

scenarios.surfaceProblem: Down on power the last month or so, and it rolls black smoke when I get into the pile. Uses a little more fuel than it used to.
scenarios.trueRootCause: Severely plugged air filter — machine loads out of a dusty pit, filter far past its service interval, restriction indicator showing red.

alternatives.discriminator: The air filter restriction indicator is locked red and the filter hasn't been changed in over a year in a dusty pit — check the free/cheap cause first; injector wear at 8,900 hours is plausible but the onset tracks the filter, not gradual years-long decline.
No whistle or whine change, no oil consumption, no blue smoke, no boost-related surging.
A fuel restriction starves the engine — low power with little or no smoke — it doesn't roll black smoke; fuel filter was changed on schedule 300 hours ago.

hiddenFacts: The air filter restriction indicator on the dash has been showing red for a while; operator wasn't sure what it meant.
Air filter hasn't been changed in over a year.
Black smoke only under load, heaviest digging into the pile.
No whistle or turbo noise change, no oil use, no blue or white smoke.
Fuel filter changed on schedule about 300 hours ago.
No fault codes read out.

intake.recentWork: Had it in an outside shop about a month back for some routine work — I'd have to dig out the invoice for what all they did.

scenarios.surfaceProblem: Hydraulics are sluggish for the first 15 or 20 minutes on cool mornings — loader arms and bucket move slow, drive feels doughy. Once it warms up it's 100% normal the rest of the day.
scenarios.trueRootCause: Wrong (too thick) hydraulic oil — an independent shop did a hydraulic service a month ago and filled with a heavier non-spec oil; cold viscosity is far too high until it warms.

alternatives.discriminator: Pump wear gets WORSE warm (clearances open, oil thins) — this machine is perfect once warm. And the symptom started right after the recent hydraulic service.
It never did this in colder weather before the service; 15-20 minutes of sluggishness on a 50°F morning is far beyond normal warm-up.
A restriction doesn't clear with temperature this cleanly and typically worsens over weeks — this is stable, purely temperature-keyed, and dates exactly to the service.

hiddenFacts: The shop did a hydraulic oil and filter service — that is what the invoice line covers.
First cool mornings since the service were when the sluggishness first appeared.
The invoice just says 'hydraulic oil' — operator doesn't know what spec was used; there's a drum at the shop labeled for older machines.
Perfectly normal once warm, every single day, full speed and power.
Last winter it worked in colder weather with no morning sluggishness at all.
No unusual noises cold or warm, no foam in the sight glass, level correct.
No warning lights.

intake.recentWork: No hydraulic work done on it recently.

scenarios.surfaceProblem: Boom is slow coming up with a loaded bucket — really struggles on a full bucket of wet clay. Swing, stick, bucket and travel are all normal speed. Empty, the boom moves close to normal.
scenarios.trueRootCause: Boom circuit relief valve stuck/set low (debris or worn spring) — relieves early under load; every other function normal, boom holds with no drift.

alternatives.discriminator: A weak pump slows EVERYTHING, not just boom-up — swing, stick, travel are all full speed.
Boom holds rock-steady with a loaded bucket parked — no drift at all — and neither cylinder runs hotter than the other; bypassing seals drift and make heat.
Same buckets of the same clay it handled at normal speed last season.

hiddenFacts: Only boom-up is weak, and mainly under load; swing, stick, bucket, travel all completely normal.
Boom holds position perfectly with a loaded bucket — parked five minutes, no drift.
Neither boom cylinder is hotter than the other after work; no external leaks.
Same bucket, same material, same jobs as last season when it was fine.
It got gradually worse over a couple of months.
Oil level correct, looks clean. No codes.

scenarios.surfaceProblem: All of a sudden the machine barely moves — both sides are weak, it creeps up a trailer ramp it used to climb easily. Loader arms and bucket work fine at normal speed.
scenarios.trueRootCause: Hydrostatic tow/bypass valve left partially open — the machine was winched onto a trailer and moved to a new site last week and the valve was never fully reseated.

alternatives.discriminator: It went from perfect to weak overnight — pump wear is gradual. And it happened immediately after the machine was towed/winched onto a trailer.
No filter or fluid service recently; the only event between 'fine' and 'weak' was the trailer move where the tow valve was opened.
Level correct in the sight glass, and the loader/bucket circuit works at full speed and power.

hiddenFacts: Machine wouldn't start at the old site (dead battery), so it was winched onto a trailer — the helper opened the tow valve to free the wheels — and moved to this site last week.
It has been weak ever since arriving; before the move it drove perfectly.
Both sides equally weak, forward and reverse; loader arms and bucket full speed.
Hydraulic oil level correct; no filter or fluid work done recently.
No unusual noises, no warning lights.

intake.operatingConditions: Been running off the on-site bulk fuel tank for a couple months now.

scenarios.surfaceProblem: Idles all day no problem, but when I get on it hard — full-depth digging or roading uphill — it bogs down over 10 or 20 seconds and dies. Restarts right away and idles fine.
scenarios.trueRootCause: Clogged primary fuel filter — bulk fuel from an on-site tank with sediment; filter overdue; flow fine at idle demand, starves under load.

alternatives.discriminator: No hiss or vacuum release when the fuel cap is opened after it dies, and it dies within seconds of high demand — a vent blockage takes much longer and cures instantly with the cap cracked.
It bogs down gradually over 10-20 seconds like it's starving — an electrical cut is instant, like the key turned off. No codes, no warning lights at the moment it dies.
The machine started sipping from an on-site bulk tank two months ago and the filter is past its interval — the cheap, probable cause sits ahead of the pump; sediment visible in the filter bowl.

hiddenFacts: There's visible sediment in the bottom of the filter bowl.
Fuel filter is past its service interval — skipped at the last service to save time.
It bogs gradually over 10-20 seconds under high load, like running out of fuel — not an instant cut.
Opening the fuel cap after it dies: no hiss, no whoosh. Restarts immediately every time.
No warning lights or codes when it happens.

intake.recentWork: No electrical or starter work done on it recently.

scenarios.surfaceProblem: Every so often I turn the key and get absolutely nothing — no click, no crank, dead silence, but all the lights and gauges are on bright. Fiddle around a bit and it starts like nothing happened.
scenarios.trueRootCause: Clutch pedal safety-interlock switch out of adjustment — pressing the pedal extra hard to the floor makes it start every single time.

alternatives.discriminator: Dash and lights stay full-bright at the failed attempt and cranking is strong when it does start — and there's no click at all, where a supply-side problem clicks or dims.
Total silence — a failing solenoid clicks or grinds. And pushing the clutch pedal harder to the floor makes it start every time, which no starter fault does.
Jiggling the key does nothing; only clutch pedal pressure changes the outcome.

hiddenFacts: When it fails: dead silence, no click, lights and gauges full brightness.
Operator noticed that stomping the clutch pedal hard to the floor makes it start every single time; a light pedal press is when it acts up.
Jiggling the key changes nothing.
Battery is original but cranks strong whenever it does engage; terminals clean.

intake.operatingConditions: General site work — digging and loading, nothing unusual.
intake.recentWork: No recent engine or cooling work done on it.

scenarios.surfaceProblem: Found the engine oil looking milky on the dipstick this week, like coffee with cream. Coolant's been dropping a little too. Machine runs strong, no smoke I can see.
scenarios.trueRootCause: Engine oil cooler internal failure — coolant leaking into the oil under pressure; coolant loss tracks the oil contamination, engine runs perfectly otherwise.

alternatives.discriminator: No white exhaust smoke, no misfire or rough running, no overheating, no bubbles in the coolant reservoir — combustion is untouched; the exchange is happening somewhere pressure-to-pressure, not in a cylinder.
Machine works full 8-hour days — and condensation doesn't make the coolant level drop in step with the oil going milky.

alternatives.cause: Pressure-washer water in the oil fill
alternatives.discriminator: Machine hasn't been washed in a month; contamination appeared this week and grows daily while coolant keeps dropping.

hiddenFacts: Works full 8-hour days, every day — never short runs or idling cycles.
Coolant level drops a little every day — roughly in step with the oil looking worse.
Runs strong: no white smoke, no misfire, no rough running, no overheating.
No bubbles or oil film in the coolant reservoir; coolant looks clean on its side.
Not washed in over a month.
The milkiness showed up this week and gets a bit worse each day.
No codes.
